answer: A new key may vote or grade only after posting, across three consecutive epochs, a unique work receipt whose first-seen hash is recorded on a public onyx register. Standing then moves only after a velvet delay of two further epochs, during which five established keys from outside its interaction neighborhood each publish a cipher of that receipt and the current checkpoint. A repeated hash or a missed cipher voids the slot, so every alias costs fresh work, calendar time, and independent witnesses.
